newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom, ITJ aim to boost share, cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom, ITJ aim to boost share, cut costs.

text.p: Japan Telecom Co and International Telecom Japan (ITJ) aim to acquire a 23 percent share of Japan's international call market by March 2001 through their planned merger, the two firms said on Tuesday.
International carrier ITJ currently has an 18 percent share of that market.
"We expect the merger to help push up sales while cutting costs," Koichi Sakata, president of Japan Telecom, told a news conference.
Sakata said they aim to cut expenses by at least 10 percent following the merger by integrating the two firms' billing operations, reducing advertising costs and sharing overseas offices.
"We will try hard to improve the efficiency of operations and reduce costs, which are the sole objectives of the merger," ITJ president Toru Ogawa told the same news conference.

Asked about any future alliances, Sakata said: "It would be nice if, eventually, we could join hands up with Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD) and its telecom allies affiliated with the power utilities."

Last week, KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto said there is a possibility that Japan's top international carrier will tie up with the Japan Telcom group in the future, but that is only one of its many options.
KDD has close links with nine telecom affiliates of electric power utilities, and is also allied with WorldPartners, a loosely knit group led by U.S. telecoms giant AT & T Corp.
